originalTitle: Trump’s municipal bond portfolio reaches as much as $1 billion as policy overlaps mount
summary: President Donald Trump disclosed municipal bond holdings worth $300 million to $1 billion, including debt tied to issuers affected by federal policy.
content:
President Donald Trump is a creditor to hundreds of cities, hospitals, schools, utilities and other public institutions across the country — many of which are directly affected by decisions made by his own administration.

And that financial exposure is growing.

Trump ended 2025 with 807 municipal bond positions worth between $240.7 million to $797.6 million, according to a CNBC analysis of his financial disclosures filed since he returned to the White House. He has since disclosed at least 243 purchases in 2026 worth between $68.2 million and $233.8 million. Among those are 48 new purchases Trump disclosed Sept. 22 when his financial report for July became public. Unlike his stock holdings, which have been actively traded during this presidency, Trump reports purchasing bonds but not selling them.

Taken together, the holdings total more than 1,000 positions valued at between $300 million and $1 billion, CNBC calculated. The exact current values are obscured because federal filings use broad ranges and exclude subsequent market moves.

"The scale of [Trump's] municipal bond exposure is unprecedented to my knowledge," said Justin Marlowe , director of the Center for Municipal Finance at the University of Chicago. "Even $100 million is large for an individual investor, and a portfolio near $1 billion functions more like an institutional fund."

In some instances, Trump held bonds tied to an issuer or facility before his administration took action affecting it. In others, his accounts bought the debt after the federal government had executed regulatory or funding actions involving the very same borrower or project.

It's the latest example of a hallmark of Trump's tenure: the fusion of executive power and personal wealth . Federal grants, regulations and healthcare funding decisions can affect the finances of issuers whose debt sits in Trump's portfolio, ethics and financial experts told CNBC.

CNBC found no evidence that Trump or his investment managers traded on advance knowledge of administration decisions, that his financial interests explicitly shaped those policies or that he directed any individual transaction.

The White House and the Trump Organization said Trump's investments are held in discretionary accounts managed by independent financial institutions .

White House spokesman Davis Ingle said neither Trump nor his family has "any ability to direct, influence, or provide input" on how the portfolio is invested or when securities are bought or sold.

A Trump Organization spokesperson similarly said the outside managers have "sole and exclusive authority" over investment decisions, including asset allocation and trading.

But outside management does not inherently eliminate questions created by holding debt from specific local governments and projects, Marlowe said. Investors seeking municipal bond exposure routinely use exchange-traded funds and other indexed products to avoid picking individual debt.

"There are lots of different ways that you can get into the market without having to pick and choose individual bonds," thereby avoiding questions about "how federal policy affects specific holdings in your portfolio," Marlowe told CNBC.

It is unclear why Trump's accounts have bought so many municipal bonds, or what role individual issuers play in the broader investment strategy. Neither the White House nor the Trump Organization provided an explanation in response to CNBC’s detailed questions about the bond purchases.

Often, wealthy investors use municipal bonds to diversify their portfolios while generating interest income that is often exempt from federal income taxes .

Trump's holdings include bonds tied to three coal-fired power plants that received relief from stricter federal pollution requirements.

In February 2025, the president's accounts bought between $50,001 and $100,000 in pollution-control bonds tied to Georgia Power's Plant Bowen . Fifty-seven days later, Trump signed a proclamation exempting dozens of coal plants — including all four Bowen units — from stricter EPA limits on toxic air pollution for two years.

Following the exemption, Trump's accounts bought up to $200,000 more in debt tied to two other covered facilities: Georgia Power's Plant Scherer and Alabama Power's James M. Barry Plant.

"The credit supporting a pollution-control bond is often dependent on the regulations governing that power plant," said Richard Painter , the former chief White House ethics lawyer for President George W. Bush and now a corporate law professor at the University of Minnesota. "If, as it seems here, a federal policy delays compliance, it swings the economics of the facility."

Trump's proclamation would have delayed compliance with the tougher standards from 2027 until 2029, though EPA ultimately repealed them in February.

"President Trump's energy secretary wouldn't be allowed to hold this type of bond, in my opinion, but because presidents are exempt from typical conflict-of-interest laws , [Trump] has," Painter told CNBC.

Trump's energy bond holdings extend beyond coal.

In July 2025, Trump signed an executive order to expedite construction and permitting for data centers as well as the infrastructure needed to power them. Four months later, his accounts began buying Omaha Public Power District electric revenue bonds, purchasing between $750,002 and $1.5 million in November and December .

S&P Global Ratings said in a November report that data centers are expected to drive the bulk of the utility's electricity-demand growth over the next three years. S&P also said continued data center expansion was integral to the utility's strategy for meeting rising debt-service obligations.

"There's a lot of power demand for data centers, and many local utilities are having to invest heavily in additional generation capacity for these data centers," said Nora Wittstruck , managing director and chief analytical officer for governments at S&P Global Ratings.

chineseTitle: 由于政策重叠加剧，特朗普的市政债券投资组合高达 10 亿美元
chineseSummary: 唐纳德·特朗普总统披露了价值 3 亿至 10 亿美元的市政债券持有量，其中包括与受联邦政策影响的发行人相关的债务。
chineseContent:
唐纳德·特朗普总统是全国数百个城市、医院、学校、公用事业和其他公共机构的债权人，其中许多机构直接受到其政府决策的影响。

而且这种财务风险正在增加。

根据 CNBC 对特朗普重返白宫后提交的财务披露的分析，截至 2025 年，特朗普持有 807 个市政债券头寸，价值在 2.407 亿美元至 7.976 亿美元之间。此后他披露了 2026 年至少 243 笔采购，价值在 6820 万美元至 2.338 亿美元之间。其中包括特朗普在 9 月 22 日公布 7 月份财务报告时披露的 48 项新采购。与他在总统任期内交易活跃的股票不同，特朗普报告购买债券但没有出售债券。

据 CNBC 计算，合计持有的头寸超过 1,000 个，价值在 3 亿至 10 亿美元之间。由于联邦文件使用了广泛的范围并排除了随后的市场波动，因此确切的当前值并不明确。

芝加哥大学市政金融中心主任贾斯汀·马洛表示：“据我所知，特朗普的市政债券敞口规模是前所未有的。” “对于个人投资者来说，即使 1 亿美元也很大，而接近 10 亿美元的投资组合更像是机构基金。”

在某些情况下，特朗普在其政府采取影响发行人或设施的行动之前就持有与该发行人或设施相关的债券。在其他情况下，他的账户在联邦政府对同一借款人或项目执行监管或融资行动后购买了债务。

这是特朗普任期标志的最新例子：行政权力与个人财富的融合。道德和金融专家告诉 CNBC，联邦拨款、监管和医疗保健融资决策可能会影响特朗普投资组合中债务的发行人的财务状况。

CNBC 没有发现任何证据表明特朗普或他的投资经理利用政府决策的预先知识进行交易，也没有证据表明他的经济利益明确影响了这些政策，或者他指导了任何个人交易。

白宫和特朗普集团表示，特朗普的投资存放在由独立金融机构管理的全权委托账户中。

白宫发言人戴维斯·英格尔表示，特朗普及其家族都没有能力“指导、影响或提供意见”投资组合的投资方式或证券的买卖时间。

特朗普集团发言人同样表示，外部经理对包括资产配置和交易在内的投资决策拥有“唯一且排他的权力”。

但马洛表示，外部管理并不能从本质上消除因持有特定地方政府和项目债务而产生的问题。寻求市政债券投资的投资者通常使用交易所交易基金和其他指数产品来避免选择个人债务。

马洛对 CNBC 表示：“你可以通过多种不同的方式进入市场，而无需挑选个别债券，”从而避免了“联邦政策如何影响你投资组合中的特定资产”的问题。

目前尚不清楚特朗普的账户为何购买了如此多的市政债券，也不清楚个别发行人在更广泛的投资策略中扮演什么角色。对于 CNBC 关于债券购买的详细问题，白宫和特朗普集团都没有做出解释。

通常，富有的投资者利用市政债券来实现投资组合多元化，同时产生通常免缴联邦所得税的利息收入。

特朗普持有的债券包括与三座燃煤电厂相关的债券，这些电厂获得了更严格的联邦污染要求的减免。

2025 年 2 月，总统的账户购买了 50,001 至 100,000 美元的与佐治亚电力公司 Bowen 工厂相关的污染控制债券。五十七天后，特朗普签署了一项公告，免除数十家燃煤电厂（包括所有四家博文电厂）两年内不受 EPA 对有毒空气污染更严格的限制。

豁免后，特朗普的账户又购买了多达 20 万美元的债务，这些债务与另外两个受保护设施相关：佐治亚电力公司的谢勒电厂和阿拉巴马电力公司的詹姆斯·M·巴里电厂。

“支持污染控制债券的信贷通常取决于管理该发电厂的法规，”乔治·W·布什总统的前首席白宫道德律师、现任明尼苏达大学公司法教授理查德·佩因特说。 “如果像这里看起来的那样，联邦政策延迟了合规性，就会影响该设施的经济状况。”

特朗普的公告将把更严格的标准从 2027 年推迟到 2029 年，尽管 EPA 最终在 2 月份废除了这些标准。

佩因特对 CNBC 表示：“在我看来，特朗普总统的能源部长不会被允许持有此类债券，但因为总统不受典型的利益冲突法的约束，所以（特朗普）持有此类债券。”

特朗普持有的能源债券不仅限于煤炭。

2025 年 7 月，特朗普签署了一项行政命令，加快数据中心及其供电所需基础设施的建设和审批。四个月后，他的账户开始购买奥马哈公共电力区电力收入债券，在 11 月和 12 月购买了 750,002 美元至 150 万美元。

标准普尔全球评级公司在 11 月份的一份报告中表示，预计数据中心将在未来三年内推动公用事业公司电力需求增长的大部分。标准普尔还表示，持续的数据中心扩张是该公用事业公司满足不断增加的偿债义务的战略的组成部分。

标准普尔全球评级公司董事总经理兼政府首席分析官诺拉·维特斯特鲁克 (Nora Wittstruck) 表示：“数据中心的电力需求很大，许多当地公用事业公司不得不大力投资为这些数据中心增加发电能力。”

CNBC 没有发现任何证据
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
